result_revision: Uncommitted diagnostic-only tooling; staging and commits remain user-owned
conclusion: The retained Intel ASan process timeout after closed was not reproduced. No causal fix or failure waiver is established.

original_failure.last_row_observations: One submitted/completed/presented frame, zero native owners, seven teardown calls, zero validation errors; no original process stack was captured.

native_diagnostic.ordering: Eight blocks of NVIDIA four faults then Intel four faults; no stress soak was present in the original regression sequence

stack_observations: Native control: SleepEx in diagnostic atexit callback and CRT execute_onexit_table.
Worker control: native child already exited; actual Python worker waits in PySemaphore_Wait and venv redirector waits in WaitForSingleObjectEx.

observer_deduplication_amendment.reason: A direct Python launch may report the same worker PID/creation time as both worker_started and worker_launched; observe each identity only once to avoid CREATE_NEW collision.
observer_deduplication_amendment.native64_rerun: NOT_RUN: no native run triggered capture; its original exact tool source and receipt remain preserved. This observer-only change was checked with fresh CPU captures.

audit_findings: Original production runner redirects stdout/stderr to temporary files, not pipes; inherited pipe EOF cannot explain its timeout.
After closed, explicit cleanup has drained/joined the graphics worker and destroyed NVRHI/Vulkan/window owners; remaining owner reset is idempotent empty cleanup.
Native/CRT/ASan/DLL shutdown and the Python launch chain remain unproven boundaries because the original run has no PID-stage or stack capture.
The separately demonstrated queue-wait thread-teardown deadline defect occurs before closed and does not explain this post-closed timeout.
limitations: Original ASAN_OPTIONS and complete host activity were not captured; exact ambient reconstruction is impossible.
Instrumentation and successful repetitions do not establish a causal fix.
Only newly added late marker functions omit ASan instrumentation; existing fixture and engine instrumentation is unchanged.
This sequence reproduces recorded adapter/fault ordering with unchanged original/current binaries, not complete original machine-wide history or a fresh preceding ASan build/CPU suite.
Original sanitizer environment was not recorded; the new run recorded no ASAN_/LSAN_/UBSAN_ variables.
The observer runner adds PID events and stage markers alter copied fixtures; unchanged original variants remain included, but successful repetitions are not a causal control.
EXE TLS callback markers prove only their own execution, not completion of every DLL detach callback.

One otherwise finite current instrumented Intel device-error exit lacks the late EXE TLS stdout marker; marker absence alone cannot identify a hang. All16 ordinary instrumented exits record owner reset, local destruction, main return, atexit and static marker destruction.
No actual GPU/device loss, host setting change, driver replacement, enlarged native deadline or healthy forced process exit was used.
